title: American Inventions: The Television

source.name: VOA Learning English — American Inventions: The Television
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Yet many people would find it difficult to name the inventor of the television. They might also be surprised to learn that the inventor came up with the idea when he was just fourteen years old.
Today, we explore the life of one of the great inventors of 20th century America: Philo Taylor Farnsworth.

Philo Farnsworth was born in August 1906, near Indian Creek in the western state of Utah. The house he lived in for the first few years of his life had no electricity. But Philo read about electricity and quickly began to experiment with it.

One night, Philo read a magazine story about the idea of sending pictures and sound through the air. The story said some of the world’s best scientists were working on the idea. It said these scientists were using special machines to try to make a kind of device to send pictures.
Fourteen-year-old Philo decided these famous scientists were wrong. He decided that mechanical devices would never work.
Philo believed such a device would have to be electronic. Philo knew electrons could be made to move very fast. All he would have to do was find a way to make electrons do the work.
Soon, Philo had an idea for such a receiver. It would trap light in a container and send the light on a line of electrons. Philo called it “light in a bottle.”
Several days later, Philo told his teacher about a device that could capture pictures. He drew a plan for it and gave it to his teacher.
Philo’s drawing seemed very simple. But it still clearly showed the information needed to build a television.

In September 1927, Philo turned on a device that was the first working television receiver. In another room was the first television camera. Philo had invented the special camera tube earlier that year.
While the image produced on the receiver was not very clear, the device worked. Within a few months, Philo had found several people who wanted to invest money in his invention.
In August 1930, the United States government gave Philo patent documents. These documents aimed to protect his invention from being copied by others.
Still, he became involved in legal disputes with a powerful company at the time known as RCA. Philo won the disputes but faced many business and financial difficulties in his life.

He developed more than 100 devices that helped make modern television possible. He also developed early radar, invented the first electronic microscope, and worked on developing peaceful uses of atomic energy.
Philo Farnsworth died in March of 1971. He is considered one of the most important inventors of the 20th century.

questions.q: Why did the young Philo disagree with the famous scientists?
options: He believed that it would never be possible to send sound as well
He thought that pictures could not be sent through the air at all
He felt that machines with moving parts could never succeed
He had tested their machines himself and found them to be dangerous
questions.explain: Đoạn 5–6: cậu cho rằng thiết bị cơ khí “would never work” và thiết bị phải là điện tử, dùng electron để làm việc.

questions.q: What was Philo’s “light in a bottle”?
options: A glass tube from a magazine that was full of electrical wires
A plan for a receiver that would hold light and send it along electrons
A machine for showing moving films on the wall of a classroom
A lamp that his family used to light the house in the evenings
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: máy thu “would trap light in a container and send the light on a line of electrons” – Philo gọi là “light in a bottle”.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about Philo’s drawing for his teacher?
options: It was unfinished and had to be completed by other scientists
It was so complicated that the teacher could not understand it at all
It had been copied carefully from a plan he found in a magazine
It looked simple, yet it included every detail required to construct a television
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: bản vẽ “seemed very simple. But it still clearly showed the information needed to build a television”.

questions.q: How good was the first working television?
options: The machine did not work properly until several months had passed
The picture was perfect, so investors were quick to give him money
The picture was clear but nobody wished to pay for the invention
The picture was poor, but the machine worked and attracted investors
questions.explain: Đoạn 10–11: hình ảnh “not very clear” nhưng thiết bị hoạt động; vài tháng sau có người muốn đầu tư.

questions.q: What happened after Farnsworth’s legal disputes with RCA?
options: He won them, but money and business problems stayed with him
He sold the invention to the company for a very large sum of money
He agreed to work for the company for the rest of his life
He lost them and was forced to give up the rights to his invention
questions.explain: Đoạn 13: “Philo won the disputes but faced many business and financial difficulties in his life.”

questions.q: What is the main message of the final paragraphs?
options: Farnsworth is better known today for radar than for anything else
Farnsworth stopped inventing as soon as he had received his patent
Farnsworth’s only important invention was the special camera tube
Farnsworth’s work reached far beyond television, and he is highly regarded
questions.explain: Đoạn 14–15: ông phát triển hơn 100 thiết bị, sơ khai về radar, kính hiển vi điện tử, năng lượng nguyên tử và được xem là một trong những nhà phát minh quan trọng nhất thế kỉ 20.

questions.q: There was electricity in the house where Philo lived as a small child.
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: ngôi nhà nơi cậu sống những năm đầu “had no electricity”.

questions.q: Philo’s teacher helped him to obtain his patent.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói cậu đưa bản vẽ cho thầy giáo; không nói thầy giúp xin bằng sáng chế.

vocab.def: to try new things to see what happens
vocab.ex: Philo read about electricity and quickly began to experiment with it.

vocab.def: a machine or tool made for a special purpose
vocab.ex: a device that could capture pictures

vocab.def: working with machines or moving parts
vocab.ex: He decided that mechanical devices would never work.

vocab.def: using electricity in very small parts such as chips
vocab.ex: Philo believed such a device would have to be electronic.

vocab.def: to take or record an image or information
vocab.ex: a device that could capture pictures

vocab.def: an official document that gives you the right to be the only one to make an invention
vocab.ex: the United States government gave Philo patent documents
he became involved in legal disputes with a powerful company

vocab.def: to put money into something to make a profit later
vocab.ex: several people who wanted to invest money in his invention

str.s: All he would have to do was + verb
str.vi: Tất cả những gì anh ấy phải làm là …
str.ex: All he would have to do was find a way to make electrons do the work.
str.explain: Cấu trúc All + (that) … + be + V nguyên mẫu (bỏ to): nhấn mạnh việc duy nhất cần làm.

str.ex: Philo believed such a device would have to be electronic.
str.explain: would là “will” ở quá khứ trong lời kể gián tiếp.

str.vi: đã … (trước một mốc quá khứ khác)
str.ex: Within a few months, Philo had found several people who wanted to invest money in his invention.
str.explain: Past perfect dùng cho việc xảy ra trước một việc/mốc thời gian trong quá khứ.

str.ex: He is considered one of the most important inventors of the 20th century.
str.explain: Bị động với consider: dùng khi nêu đánh giá chung.
